name: Fibroblast growth factor (FGF)
lead: Fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) are a family of 23 signaling proteins in humans that regulate cell growth, tissue organization and wound healing, signaling through four receptor types (FGFR1-4).[1] FGF2, also called basic FGF (bFGF), promotes blood vessel formation, fibroblast proliferation and granulation tissue in wound repair.[1] Topical FGF is included in some anti-aging serums.

Wikipedia states that FGF2 has been shown to enhance tissue repair in clinical settings such as burns, skin grafts and ulcers, and lists trafermin, a recombinant FGF2 drug, among FGF receptor agonists.[1] The sources reviewed contain no trials of topical FGF serums for wrinkles or skin aging.

paras: Most FGFs act locally, binding heparan sulfate in the extracellular matrix and being released during injury or tissue remodeling, while FGF15/19, FGF21 and FGF23 act as hormones.[1] FGF2 is also involved in neural stem cell activity.[1]

No studies found of topical FGF serums for appearance or anti-aging. Medical uses of FGF2 in burns, grafts and ulcers are described in general terms on Wikipedia.[1] Other human studies found in the sources measure circulating FGF levels in disease (for example serum bFGF in hemangioma or lymphoma patients) and do not test FGF as a treatment.[2][3]

Wikipedia notes that overactive FGF signaling is linked to several diseases and that FGF-signaling inhibitors have shown clinical benefit in some of them.[1] Circulating bFGF levels have been measured as an angiogenic marker in blood cancers.[4] The sources reviewed do not report safety data for cosmetic FGF use.

card.note: Overactive FGF signaling is linked to disease; no cosmetic safety data found.

quick.overview:
FGFs are a family of signaling proteins that drive cell growth and wound repair. FGF2 (bFGF) is the form most often discussed for skin, and some anti-aging serums contain growth factors of this type.

No trials of topical FGF serums for aging skin were found.
quick.mechanism: FGFs bind receptors on cells and promote fibroblast proliferation, blood vessel formation and granulation tissue in wound healing.
quick.risks: Overactive FGF signaling is associated with several diseases. Safety of cosmetic use was not covered in the sources reviewed.
